subject: ventures/moving-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a local moving company who prices jobs hourly (crew-hours with a minimum, plus truck, fuel, valuation coverage), checking first that hours x crew x loaded wage ties to a bid and that margin is on price

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid via node on a hand-built job (1 row 1100 cu ft/5h; 3 dest flights @8min; 80ft carry @6min/50ft; 2 drive h; crew 3; $25 wage +20% burden; truck 150, fuel 60, materials 40; overhead 10%; margin 20%). Hand arithmetic: factor 5.5; stairs 3*(8/60)*5.5=2.2h; carry 1.6*0.1*5.5=0.88h; clock 10.08h (tool 10.08); person-h 30.24 x $30 = $907.20 (tool 907.2); direct 1157.20, +10% = 1272.92 (tool 1272.92); price 1272.92/0.8 = $1591.15 (tool 1591.15). Proposed $1200: profit -72.92, margin -6.08% (hand: (1200-1272.92)/1200 = -6.077%) and belowBreakEven true. Also checked margin-on-price identity (price*(1-m)=cost) and the 200 cu ft basis scaling. Inputs are the author's own assumptions, not an external standard; the formulas match the cost-plus identities in standard small-business pricing (margin = profit/price).
evidence.completeness: Claimed and exercised through module/tests: inventory hours, volume-scaled stairs/carry, flat elevator wait, packing, drive, loaded labour, overhead, margin-on-price, walk-away price, bedroom-count quote check, share link, proposal, SEO pages (how-much-to-charge, vs-*), usage opt-out. Tests cover all of these (116 pass). I did not render index.html in a browser; page.test.mjs checks the markup and scripts as text.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/moving-bid-calculator && node --test calc.test.mjs proposal.test.mjs share.test.mjs usage.test.mjs page.test.mjs (and plain node --test): 116 pass, 0 fail. Seeded mutation: calc.mjs price = totalCost / (1 - m/100) changed to totalCost * (1 + m/100): 3 tests failed (caught). Reverted with git checkout.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (194 lines), llms.txt, README, index.html head/FAQ. Pure, DOM-free, validated inputs with named errors, frozen presets, no silent fallbacks except documented defaults. Defects: input.name?.trim() fallback to 'Item N' fine; llms.txt still points to the old github.io address; proposedPrice===0 margin silently 0; no rounding of price to cents/dollars.
evidence.claims: README formula steps 1-7 match calc.mjs:112-139 line by line; 'walk-away price' = totalCost (calc.mjs:176); disclaimer present in README and page; 'not an industry standard' on presets stated. Weakness: llms.txt lists duncan-haywood.github.io URLs while README says marisstella.app (stale but redirected per CLAUDE.md).
evidence.fitness: A mover can price a job and test a competitor quote. Gaps in the first hour: local moves are usually billed as an hourly rate with a 2-3 hour minimum, and the tool outputs only a lump sum plus effective hourly per mover, not a billable crew rate; no line for cargo valuation/liability coverage, no per-mile travel charge, no tax; drive hours are charged at the full crew rate.
evidence.domain: A mover would compare against hourly crew-rate quoting with minimums, and the industry-standard weight-based (7 lb/cu ft) tariff for long distance (out of scope, stated). The access-by-volume idea is sound; margin-on-price is correct. Preset hours are unsourced ballparks, labelled as such. Departs by not producing the billable hourly rate/minimum or valuation cost.

defects.what: Output is a lump-sum price only; no billable crew hourly rate or minimum-hours output, and no valuation/liability coverage cost line, which is how local moves are quoted and where they lose money
llms.txt links the old github.io address, not marisstella.app
Preset clock hours and cubic feet are unsourced ballparks (labelled as such)

verdict: Arithmetic is correct (four outputs recomputed by hand match), tests are strong (116 pass; a margin-formula mutation failed 3 tests) and claims match the code. It stops at a lump-sum cost-plus number: an owner would still need to convert it to an hourly rate with minimum and add valuation coverage, so it is a sound worksheet short of senior-practitioner fitness and domain fit. Meets the bar by the computed rule; the median of seven is 3.
